seen_animation: Frames 1-6: a lion doodle lies on a ground line, body stretched left with a hump-backed outline and two leg loops, head (oval face, smile, spiky mane) at center-right facing right; the grey cloud and tree shift slightly left frame to frame, so the view pans right while the lion stays nearly in the same place. Frame 7: the lion has moved toward the right edge. Frame 8: only the lion's back and the left half of its head remain at the right edge, and a small spiky shape enters at the left edge with a grey tree outline. Frames 9-10: a second lion is shown at the left as a round frontal face with a smile surrounded by radial spikes, with a vertical line below it; the first lion's body sits at the right edge. Frame 11: the second lion's head is redrawn as a right-facing oval with an eye at its right side, the spikes now only to the left of the head and broken into separate pieces. Frame 12: the head faces right in profile, the mane is a jagged band to the left, the body below is faint and partly missing. Frames 13-16: the second lion lies in profile at left, body extending off the left edge, head facing right, with the first lion's back still visible at the right edge; little change across these four frames.
seen_film: Frames 1-4: a white male lion lies on a rock ledge in front of foliage, head turned right in profile, body extending left. Frames 5-8: the camera pans right; the lion moves to the right side of the frame and by frame 8 only its back and partial head show at the right edge, while a birch tree and the edge of a second lion's mane appear at the left. Frames 9-10: a second lion lies at the left, facing the camera with its face frontal, while the first lion's back is visible at the right. Frames 11-12: the second lion turns its head to its left (screen right) through a three-quarter view into profile. Frames 13-16: the second lion lies in right-facing profile left of center, the first lion's rump at the right edge; the shot holds.
named_subject: A lion lying down (two lions in sequence: the first passes out of frame right during a pan, the second faces camera and then turns its head to profile).
evidence: Placement and timing follow the film: frames 1-6 lion center-right with head right as in film 1-6; frame 8 first lion cut by the right edge with a mane edge entering left, matching film 8; frames 9-10 frontal face at left matching the film's frontal second lion; frames 12-16 profile head left of center with the first lion's back at right, matching film 12-16. The weakness is the head turn: between frame 10 (round frontal face with radial spikes all around) and frame 11 (oval profile-leaning face with spikes only on the left, broken into separate fragments) the head is replaced by a differently constructed drawing rather than rotated, and in frame 12 the body below the head is faint and partially missing before it reappears fully in frame 13. The film shows this turn as one gradual head rotation over frames 10-12 with the body constant. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The second lion's head turn in frames 10-12 is a swap from a frontal sun-face drawing to a profile drawing, with the mane fragmenting and the body dropping out, instead of one continuous rotation of the same head.
closes_when: Frames 10, 11 and 12 show the same head outline and mane strokes progressively rotating (frontal, three-quarter with the face features shifted right and the mane spikes thinning on the right side, then profile), with the mane drawn as continuous strokes and the body outline present at full weight in every frame.
protect: The timing and frame positions that match the film (static lion 1-6, exit right at 7-8, second lion entering left at 8, frontal at 9-10, profile hold 13-16, first lion's back kept at the right edge from 9 to 16); the c.png construction of the lying lion (hump-back outline, two leg loops, oval face with small smile, flicked spiky mane strokes); the sparse grey scenery panning with the camera.
identity_gap: The first lion and the second lion in frames 13-16 are the c.png drawing, but the frontal sun-shaped face in frames 9-10 is a new construction not in the doodle and does not carry over into the profile head, so the second lion reads as two different drawings during its turn.
